label: sequence began with f: late original-phase steps and <DEL>
explanation: Fires on sequences whose first original token is f (95% of activation mass), from step 4 of the original phase through the <DEL> step. It is silent at steps 0-3 and never fires in the copy phase. Within a sequence the activation rises across the original phase and usually peaks a step or two before <DEL>, then drops somewhat at <DEL>. The strongest examples (all top 12) start with f f, so a second f appears to amplify it. The current input token has almost no effect. Missed activations are weak (5.5% of mass) and mostly come from sequences with f at position 1 instead of 0. False positives are mainly short sequences at step 4/<DEL> where the feature stays near zero.

issues: Count recall is only 0.76 (test). About 12% of active steps come from sequences with f at position 1 rather than position 0 (predicate (first_tok!=f)&(orig(1)==f)&(t>=4)&(phase<=1): P 0.16, R 0.12, mass 0.039). This weak secondary mode is real, and the explanation already discloses it. Adding it to the predicate lowers F1: 0.692 with t>=4, 0.798 with t>=6.
'Silent at steps 0-3' is slightly overstated. t=3 has 388 active dev steps (0.1% of mass), so it is negligible but not zero.
The remaining ~11% of active count is scattered across sequences with no f in positions 0-1 (P 0.005, mass 0.015). This looks like weak noise, not a systematic class.
False positives (2083 test steps, P 0.964) are mostly f-first sequences at step 4 or <DEL> in short sequences, matching the explanation. An L>=5 restriction did not improve F1 (0.838 vs 0.850).

Checks that held up: zero activation in the copy phase (dev profile: copy 0 active, recall_idx>=1 all 0). first_tok=f carries 94.6% of mass. The current input token has a flat effect (lift ~0.9-1.0x for all non-DEL tokens). The top examples show the activation peaking a step or two before <DEL> and dropping at <DEL>.
